propositions.claim: The substituted imprisonment is limited by the order's own words to the duration of the war. This limit attaches to the imprisonment only; it does not show completion of the transport orders or of any other instruction.
propositions.quote: be mitigated to imprisonment during the war

propositions.claim: Commanding generals with power to act on court-martial proceedings 'in such cases' are authorized in special cases to restore sentenced deserters to duty. review.conclusion_reason: OPEN is justified because the disposition and scope of the restore-to-duty authority and forwarding obligation remain unresolved, and no current operating source is established. Formal status can be reported only as no express ending verified in these materials. This does not uphold the clause-level ending dates: the imprisonment duration does not establish expiry or performance of the additional discharge and forfeiture instruction. The accepted-original assertion also fails verification.
missed_evidence: The cited APP transcription, paragraph 2 (https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/executive-order-deserters-death-sentences-remitted), retains 'in such cases'; the authority's scope cannot be assessed solely from the shortened quotation in p4.

The worker's own p7–p8 quotations distinguish an additional discharge instruction from imprisonment 'during the war'. Even if verified, those quotations would not support the amendment clause's asserted 1866 expiry; performance or another ending source is missing.
review.stop_code_verdict: wrong (WEB fits the expressly identified but unread 27 May 1865 candidate; NOT_FOUND is premature). The evidence slice supplies only a compilation lead, which was also inaccessible during review, and does not establish exhaustion of the named later-order sources.
review.suspected_defect: The discharge-and-forfeiture clause is marked ended by 1866-08-20 using a duration attached to imprisonment. That transfers an expiry condition to a separate instruction without supporting text or evidence of performance; whether intentional cannot be determined.
